note:
**The meaning of the verses**
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتًا غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّىٰ تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَىٰ أَهْلِهَا ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: do not enter houses other than your own until you ask their people's permission to enter and greet them with salam. The wording of this from the Sunnah is: "As-salamu alaykum, may I come in?" Asking permission is better for you, so that by doing it you may remember Allah's commands and obey Him.

﴿فَإِن لَّمْ تَجِدُوا فِيهَا أَحَدًا فَلَا تَدْخُلُوهَا حَتَّىٰ يُؤْذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ وَإِن قِيلَ لَكُمُ ارْجِعُوا فَارْجِعُوا ۖ هُوَ أَزْكَىٰ لَكُمْ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ عَلِيمٌ﴾

If you find no one in other people's houses, do not enter them until someone is there to give you permission. And if they do not give permission, but say to you, "Go back," then go back and do not insist, for going back then is purer for you, because a person has situations he does not want anyone to see. And Allah knows what you do, and will reward everyone for his deeds.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. What did Joud use to do in the neighbours' houses? And why did Taym say nothing when he found his bike by Joud's door?
2. What happened in Uncle Abu Nader's yard? And what did Joud remember when he found his sister Zeina in his room?
3. If we knock on the door and they do not give us permission, should we get upset? (No, we go back content, as Grandma said; the person in the house might be asleep or ill.) And is asking permission only for houses? (No, we also ask permission before taking what is not ours, just as Joud asked Taym's permission for his bike.)

**This week's exercise**
This week, make a "door rule" at home: no one goes into someone else's room until they knock, say salam and are given permission, grown-ups before children; and no one takes their brother's or sister's toy or things until they ask permission.
